newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Up, Taiwan record mogas buy.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Up, Taiwan record mogas buy.

text.p: Light distillates in Singapore drifted up on Thursday, despite softer crude and a build in stocks, traders said.
Light distillate stocks, comprised gasoline, reformate and naphtha, rose 615,000 barrels to 5.634 million barrels int he week ended March 5.

But the market shrugged off the stock data as Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) made a bullish record award in its import tender for 250,000 barrels each of leaded and unleaded 95-octane reformate.
CPC awarded the tender close to $29.00 per barrel for the April 1-15 deliveries, c-and-f Taiwan.
"It is a very attractive number for the seller," a major said. In its last tender, CPC had bought two unleaded cargoes for March 16-30 delivery at $27.90 and $28.20 c-and-f.
Market sources said the winner was a South Korean refiner but CPC officials declined to divulge details.

In the Singapore fob market, a major offered 92-octane unleaded cargoes in March at $28.90 per barrel, but found no buyers. The last deal on the grade, on Monday, was at $28.20 for 80,000-barrels lifting March 19-23.
Premiums were assessed at 50-70 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, with a major rumoured covering a very prompt requirement at 90 cents.
A Japanese trader was also heard to have bought an end March 92-octane unleaded cargo at around 15 cents fob Thailand over Singapore quotes, but the seller, a Thai refiner, denied the deal.
Short term gasoline prices have peaked as current high Singapore prices have boosted reformer output, while regional shutdowns and shortfalls should ease in April, some traders said.
Naphtha edged up as the market continued to shake off the arbitrage cargo jitters amid fresh regional demand.
CPC tendered to buy 30,000 tonnes of full-range naphtha for delivery April 1-30 to Kaohsiung, a company official said. The tender closes March 10 and is valid until March 12.
CPC's last full-range purchase for March 11-20 delivery was at $239-$240 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis.
A Thai aromatics company covered its requirement of 25,000 tonnes of full-range naphtha for end March delivery on Wednesday, but details were p+c.
Another Thai petrochemical is meanwhile seeking 35,000 tonnes of light naphtha for mid-April, its first spot import requirement, a company source said.
April swaps firmed by around 20 cents per barrel to $22.50/$22.75.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
